…d by Stan Szucik, running his first 20, but with such notable personalities as Ron Clark, Geoff Iden, Bill McMinnis and Harry Hicks in the field, this rashness of an inexperienced runner eventually led to his retirement.…

At that time I was out on the marathon course and saw Ron Clark and Fred Norris run themselves to a standstill and finally retire, to leave Harry Hicks gamely battling on to the finish, although being attacked with cramp on the track.

He eventually finished 39th, ahead of international Harry Hicks and many other performers of high rank. Next man was Charlie Walker, 77th, an improvement on recent form, with ever consistant Eric Gebbett 134th.

What names there are to recall in that piece - Harry Hicks became a team mate in 1956, Gordon Pirie a friend from the same time and then Walter Hesketh who was a Fascist election candidate for the area I was responsible for in Manchester!
